chain.label: MD-11 light control force characteristics / relaxed longitudinal stability at high-altitude cruise
chain.trigger: the light control force characteristics of the MD-11 airplane in high altitude cruise flight

chain.label: DAC/China Airlines training and flight manuals did not address high-altitude upset recovery
chain.trigger: neither DAC nor China Airlines had addressed the issue of high altitude upsets in their training or flight manuals

chain.label: Pilot lacked training specific to recovery from high-altitude, high-speed upsets
chain.trigger: a lack of pilot training specific to the recovery from high altitude, high speed upsets in the MD-11

caused_by.evidence: neither DAC nor China Airlines had addressed the issue of high altitude upsets in their training or flight manuals

chain.label: Airplane encountered light-to-moderate turbulence at FL330
chain.trigger: the airplane entered an area of light turbulence...the turbulence increased to moderate

chain.label: Moderate lateral gust from the left struck the airplane, inducing the upset
chain.trigger: a 0.25 G lateral acceleration to the right was recorded...consistent with a gust from the left side of the airplane

caused_by.evidence: flight CI-012 encountered moderate turbulence that preceded the violent motions of the airplane

chain.label: Pilot applied excessive wheel and control column deflections
chain.trigger: the pilot commanded excessive control column deflections concurrent with the excessive wheel deflections

caused_by.evidence: the initial deviation from cruise flight was the result of a lateral gust from the left side of the airplane
the initial overcontrol was the result of the light control forces inherent in the MD-11 design
the pilot's response to the stall warning was also not appropriate

chain.label: Airplane entered at least four aerodynamic stalls during the recovery
chain.trigger: indicated that the airplane stalled and pitched down...at least four times during the recovery

caused_by.evidence: the control column deflections resulted in rapidly increasing AOA and pitch angles

chain.label: Pilot ignored stall warning and retrimmed nose-up against recommended procedure
chain.trigger: the pilot chose to ignore the stall warning system...the pilot applied ANU trim during the climb

caused_by.evidence: the pilot had to override the 50-pound control column force to maintain the airplane in a stalled condition for about 2 minutes and 45 seconds

chain.label: Airplane departed controlled flight with severe pitch/roll excursions for about 10 minutes
chain.trigger: the airplane suddenly began a series of pitch and roll maneuvers that lasted for about 10 minutes...both the pitch and bank exceeded 30 degrees

caused_by.evidence: the stall warning was activated most of the time between 4 and 170 seconds following the initial upset
the continued increase in pitch and AOA contributed to the first stall break

chain.label: Buffet loads during the stall recovery exceeded the elevators' design limit load
chain.trigger: the elevator skin separation probably resulted from overstress produced during the stall buffet, when the elevators were loaded above the design limit load

caused_by.evidence: the aircraft reached a 20 percent buffet boundary exceedence...more than 20 percent above the buffet boundary for 27.1 seconds

chain.label: Elevator skins fractured, delaminated, and portions separated from the airplane
chain.trigger: sustained damage to the left and right outboard elevator skin assemblies, portions of which separated from the airplane

caused_by.evidence: the separation of the elevator skin most likely occurred during the stall buffet when the elevators were loaded above the design limit load

chain.label: Pilot regained control; airplane continued and landed uneventfully with no injuries despite elevator damage
chain.trigger: airplane control was established about 3 minutes after the initial upset...the airplane continued on and landed uneventfully at Anchorage, Alaska

caused_by.evidence: airplane control was established about 3 minutes after the initial upset when the elevators were returned to neutral and the speed increased to above 200 KIAS
there was no other damage...none of whom reported any injuries
